text:
anya: Heads-up — saw a nasty perf regression on a TP+PP run after the remat alignment change. Production 8-GPU job p99 token latency jumped ~2.3x and all-reduce time dominated.
martin: Ugh. I reproduced on a smaller run yesterday. Remat seems to be creating extra cross-stage synchronization points; KV cache warmup gets fragmented.
leo: I ran a quick profile. Posting the perf-bot summary below.
perf-bot: profiling summary (rprof v2):
```
model=opt-30b, config=tp=2,pp=4,seq=2048,batch=1
before: avg_allreduce=48ms, p99_allreduce=58ms, batching_window=40ms
after(remat-align): avg_allreduce=118ms, p99_allreduce=142ms, batching_window=12ms
kernel_selector: fallback to generic_matmul for big-seq (>1024) in 18% of matmuls
kv_cache: observed 3x more KV re-alloc/flush events per token range
comm/compute overlap: reduced by ~60% due to earlier sync points
```
jen: That kernel_selector fallback line is suspicious. Did we push any heuristics that penalize fused matmul for remat cases? I remember a change to avoid aggressive fusion across remat boundaries.
martin: Yep, commit 0a1b2c3 adjusted fusion heuristics to avoid cache pollution when remat_enabled=true. We probably over-corrected — it pushes smaller kernels that serialize.
anya: Repro steps I'm using:
```
rprof --job tp=2,pp=4 --model redwood/opt-30b --seq 2048 --remat align_on_chunk --trace comm,kvcache,kernel_selector
# example log excerpt
[KVCACHE] flush boundary triggered at remat_chunk=3, evicting stage-key for shard 1
[ALL-REDUCE] start shard=1 size=8MB t=112.3ms
```
leo: Quick experiment: forcing kernel_selector to prefer cuBLAS_fused for large matmuls reduced p99_allreduce by ~35% on the repro job. Compute increased slightly but net latency down ~15%.
jen: So two things: remat alignment is creating more, smaller all-reduces, and a kernel fallback is making each all-reduce take longer (less opportunity for overlap). Both amplify.
martin: Proposed short-term fixes: 1) tweak kernel_selector priority for remat paths; 2) increase batching window heuristics when pp>1 to coalesce micro-allreduces; 3) avoid per-remat-chunk KV flush if we can preserve KV across the PP boundary.
anya: Sounds good. Which patch do we land first? Reordering could mask root cause.
martin: I'll open two PRs: (A) kernel_selector heuristic tweak — small and low-risk, (B) batching_window adaptive increase for pp pipelines — medium risk, needs perf tests. Also adding a debug metric for "kv_flush_count_per_epoch".
leo: Add a micro-benchmark in eng-runtime/bench that reproduces remat boundary fragmentation. I already have a minimal script, will attach in the PR.
perf-bot: queued CI perf job: perf/regression/pp-tp-remat-kv-bisect -> baseline=1991000000, candidate=0a1b2c3->HEAD
ci-bot: nightly perf test will run with extra tracing for kvcache/allreduce/kernels.
jen: If kernel tweak doesn't fully recover, plan B is to alter remat alignment to keep KV lifetime contiguous across PP stage boundaries. That's higher risk but probably the clean fix.
anya: Agree. For rollout, if any canary shows >1.5x regression we hold. Tagging @eng-sre and adding notes to the runbook.
martin: Filing issue: GH #4823 "remat-align -> all-reduce amplification + kernel fallback" with repro and perf traces. Will link PRs and perf runs.
leo: Thanks — I'll help with the benchmark and the PR reviews. :thumbsup:
anya: Great work. Let's keep updates in this thread when PRs land and perf runs complete.
